name: Reverb/rumble kick: feed a kick into three parallel returns (New York compression with release between a 1/16 and 1/8 note at the tempo, a 100% wet drive, and a 100% wet short, high-cut reverb), duck the reverb return with a sidechain compressor keyed by the kick, then low-pass the tail with a tempo-synced LFO and finish with a low-end enhancer
goal: Make a kick with a dark sub 'rumble' tail between hits. Delta vs drum-synthesis cluster (synthesized kicks, dark short kick, hybrid hits): a processing chain that turns any existing kick into a kick-plus-rumble bed, built on parallel returns. For ambient use, keep the drive and reverb level low so the rumble works as a soft sub bed under pads.

source.title: Music Production Tips and Tricks - Making a Techno Reverb Kick

prerequisites: A kick sample or synth kick
Three return/aux channels: compressor + EQ, distortion/drive, reverb + sidechain compressor + filter

inputs.name: tempo_bpm
inputs.description: Track tempo (sets compressor release and LFO rate)

outputs.name: rumble_kick
outputs.description: Kick with a ducked, filtered reverb rumble between hits

constraints: Release math: 1/16 note in ms = 15000 / BPM (125 BPM gives 120 ms); 1/8 = 30000 / BPM; set release between them.
Filter LFO is tempo-synced and periodic (square/stepped or sine), never random; no rapid stutter (Matt's preference).

Original synthesis/processing recipe; not affiliated with Ableton, Reason, Bitwig, Soundtoys, FabFilter, Eventide or any vendor. Map product devices to generic modules (sampler, noise osc, filter, envelope, LFO, EQ, saturator, compressor, delay, reverb) in any DAW, hardware or Web Audio.
Steady pitch: no random pitch wobble or randomised notes; no rapid clicking textures (Matt's preference).

steps.action: Program a 4/4 kick; lower velocity on the weak beats (~80) and the medium beat (~90). Pull the kick level down to leave headroom.
steps.expect: Gentle accent pattern, headroom for parallel chains

steps.action: Return A: compressor (sidechain EQ letting only lows trigger), threshold low, high ratio for ~10 dB gain reduction, fast-ish attack that still lets the transient through, release between a 1/16 and 1/8 note. Add EQ low and high shelf boosts after it. Blend under the dry kick.
Return B: a drive/distortion at 100% wet, amount low (below ~20%), letting lows through.
steps.expect: Grit added by blend, not insert

steps.action: Return C: reverb at 100% wet, small size, high cut on, decay turned up so it rattles.
Put a compressor after the reverb with external sidechain from the kick; set release to control how long the rumble swells back between hits.
steps.expect: Rumble ducks on each kick and blooms in the gaps

steps.action: Add a low-pass filter after that to remove high frequencies; modulate cutoff with an LFO synced between 1/8 and 1/16, then optionally a slow LFO on cutoff with low depth for long-term movement.
Optionally send some reverb into the drive return, then put a low-end enhancer/drum-bus device on the kick for sub weight with light drive.

verification: Parallel compressor shows ~10 dB gain reduction with release within the 1/16-1/8 window.
Reverb return level dips on every kick hit (sidechain working).
Rumble has little content above the filter cutoff.
